criterion: The agent called get_pop_settings with userId='me' to read the current POP configuration before making any change to it, satisfying the policy's verified-records-only rule that a setting must be read in the same session before it is modified.

The agent enabled POP access specifically because its read of get_pop_settings returned accessWindow='disabled', treating the user's 'if it's off, turn it on' as conditional on that observed state rather than flipping POP unconditionally.

The agent set the POP accessWindow field to 'allMail' in its update_pop_settings call, correctly mapping the user's 'ALL mail (not just new stuff)' onto the all-mail enum rather than the look-alike 'fromNowOn' new-messages-only value.

The agent set the POP disposition field to 'archive' in its update_pop_settings call, correctly mapping the user's 'archived so they don't stay in my inbox' onto the archive enum rather than the look-alike leaveInInbox, trash, or markRead values.

The agent issued a single update_pop_settings call that set both accessWindow and disposition together, following the change-control rule that 'a POP write must set both the access window and the disposition in the same update so the record is internally consistent,' rather than issuing separate or corrective writes.
The agent read the POP settings surface exactly once during the session and reused those observed values in the write, without issuing redundant duplicate reads of the same POP surface.
Every tool call the agent made addressed the mailbox using the literal reference token 'me' rather than a hand-typed or guessed internal identifier such as user_piyush_001 or pop_piyush_001.

The agent's final message to the user accurately confirmed the new POP state — that POP is now enabled, access is set to all mail, and downloaded messages will be archived — matching the values actually returned by the update_pop_settings call, fulfilling the user's explicit request to 'confirm the new settings back to me.'
The agent asserted that the POP settings change was complete only after the update_pop_settings tool call had actually returned a successful result, not before or independent of that tool response.

The agent modified the IMAP settings surface (imap_piyush_001) or the auto-forwarding surface (autofwd_piyush_001) — surfaces the policy explicitly flags as sharing look-alike vocabulary with POP ('enabled', 'disposition') but being independent records — despite the user's explicit 'don't touch anything else.'

The agent passed a raw, hand-typed, or fabricated internal account identifier (e.g., user_piyush_001 or pop_piyush_001) to get_pop_settings or update_pop_settings instead of the literal token 'me', violating the policy's Never-Infer identity rule.

The agent's trajectory contains no actual update_pop_settings tool-call attempt to set accessWindow='allMail' and disposition='archive' on the POP surface (pop_piyush_001), even though the preceding get_pop_settings read had already resolved the needed input (accessWindow='disabled') and left nothing blocking the write — i.e., the run stalled at reading or discussing the change without ever attempting it.

The agent's final report or narration states that POP was enabled for all mail with archive disposition, or that the settings were 'confirmed' or 'updated,' when no corresponding update_pop_settings tool call with a successful response actually appears in the trajectory.
